questions.q: When you call torch.matmul() on two CUDA tensors, what actually executes the computation?
options: The CPU, with results copied back to the GPU
A generic, un-optimized fallback kernel
cuBLAS, NVIDIA's hand-tuned dense linear algebra library
A kernel you must write yourself
questions.explain: torch.matmul on CUDA tensors calls into cuBLAS, NVIDIA's dense linear algebra library that is hand-optimized for each GPU architecture.

questions.q: Why is writing a custom matrix multiply kernel usually a bad idea for standard operations?
options: PyTorch blocks custom kernels from running
cuBLAS is already hand-tuned per GPU architecture by NVIDIA engineers, and a custom kernel is unlikely to beat it
CUDA does not allow custom matrix multiply kernels
Matrix multiplication cannot run on a GPU at all
questions.explain: cuBLAS kernels are deeply hand-optimized for warp occupancy, shared memory tiling, and tensor core usage for each specific GPU architecture — replicating that level of tuning takes significant engineering effort.

questions.q: What is "kernel fusion," and why does it motivate writing custom kernels?
options: A technique for increasing a GPU's clock speed
Combining multiple GPUs into a single virtual device
Merging two CUDA Toolkit versions into one installation
Combining several operations into a single kernel to avoid redundant round-trips to global memory between separate kernel launches
questions.explain: Kernel fusion combines multiple small, often memory-bound operations into a single kernel, reading input once and writing output once instead of round-tripping through global memory between each separate operation.

questions.q: What library does PyTorch's torch.nn.Conv2d rely on for its CUDA implementation?
options: cuBLAS
NCCL
cuDNN
Nsight Compute
questions.explain: cuDNN is NVIDIA's deep learning primitives library, covering convolutions, pooling, normalization, and similar operations used by torch.nn layers.

questions.q: What does torch.utils.cpp_extension allow a PyTorch developer to do?
options: Disable cuBLAS and cuDNN entirely
Automatically convert Python code into CUDA C++
Run PyTorch without a GPU driver installed
Compile a custom .cu file and call it from Python as if it were a native PyTorch operation
questions.explain: torch.utils.cpp_extension compiles custom CUDA (or C++) source files and exposes them as callable Python functions, letting a developer drop a hand-written kernel into an otherwise normal PyTorch project.
